title: Aryeo capability manifest
description: Describes one generation of the Aryeo API the way it actually responds. Every client in this repository is generated from a document conforming to this schema.

generation.description: Which Aryeo API this document describes. Clients select a generation at construction; the domain surface is identical across them.

perPageMax.description: Server-side ceiling. Requesting more is accepted and silently capped, so clients must not promise a larger page.

filterStyle.description: bracketed means filter[name]=value. Flat parameters are ignored on this generation.

enumCase.description: Case filter enum values are sent in. Response enums may use a different case; that is recorded per operation.

operations.description: Keyed by domain operation id, e.g. orders.list. The id is stable across generations and is what the generated clients expose.

path.description: Path template relative to baseUrl. Parameters in {braces}.

mutates.description: True for anything that changes upstream state. Mutating operations are generated behind the confirmation gate and are never invoked by the probe tooling.

filters.description: Query filters. The state field is the point of this whole document.

params.description: Non-filter query parameters, e.g. timezone, interval, page.

body.description: Request body fields for mutating operations.

includes.description: Relationship expansions this endpoint accepts, taken verbatim from the allowlist the API returns in a 400 body. An empty array means expansions are not supported here; omit the key when unknown.

includesUnvalidated.description: True when the endpoint accepts unknown includes with a 200 instead of returning an allowlist, so its real expansions cannot be discovered from outside. Clients expose no include parameter in that case.

sorts.description: Accepted sort fields. Prefix with - for descending.

responseEnums.description: Values a field can hold in a response. Recorded separately from filter values because the two frequently disagree in case and in membership.

quirks.description: Behaviour a caller would otherwise discover in production. One sentence each, plain language.

exercisedHere.description: False when the contract is known from production usage but no request has been fired from this repository. A fact about us, not about the API.

state.description: available: the contract is known and the operation is callable. unauthorised: the route exists but the API refuses it with a standard key. absent: the route does not exist. unverified: the contract itself is not known, so calling it would be guesswork. A write whose contract is known from production usage is available and gated by confirmation, not blocked.

alternative.description: Operation id to reach for instead when this one is unusable.

confirmation.description: How a caller proves intent before a mutating call runs. A boolean flag is deliberately not an option: a prompt with one safe answer and one dangerous answer gets answered by reflex.

kind.description: echoIdentifier: the caller must supply a value read off the target record, so the record has to have been fetched first.

field.description: Which field of the target record must be echoed back, e.g. number.

warns.description: What the caller should be told before this runs, in terms of what the customer sees.

wire.description: Exact query parameter sent. Omit for a filter that is never sent, such as an ignored one.

state.description: honoured: measured with a real value and the result set narrowed. ignored: accepted with a 200 and no effect, so the caller gets everything back looking filtered. rejected: the API refuses it outright. unverified: not yet measured.

arrayForm.description: indexed means filter[name][0]=value. Several Aryeo filters accept only the plural indexed form and ignore the singular spelling entirely.

useInstead.description: For an ignored or rejected filter, the name of the one that does work.

strategy.description: What the client does with a filter the API will not apply. client-side means it is applied in memory over a bounded scan and reported in the response. unsupported means it is not exposed at all.

evidenceRef.description: Where the claim came from. Every honoured or ignored filter should carry one.

measurement.description: The number that settled it, e.g. 1 of 5383.

source.description: probe: measured by the probe tool. production: read out of code that has been running against a live account, which is how mutating operations are described.
